nodes.summary: `(α + β)^{(n)} = ∑_{k ≤ n} C(n, k) α^{(k)} β^{(n - k)}`, for all real `α, β`.
nodes.title: Chu–Vandermonde identity for rising factorials

nodes.summary: Beta-binomial mass `C(n, k) α^{(k)} β^{(n - k)} / (α + β)^{(n)}` (zero for `k > n`, since `C(n, k) = 0`). A probability mass function for `α, β > 0`.
nodes.title: Beta-binomial mass function

nodes.summary: Bursty expression stationary law (Shahrezaei–Swain). For burst rate `κ > 0`, decay rate `γ > 0` and mean burst size `b ≥ 0`, the negative binomial law with size `a = κ / γ` (bursts per lifetime) and mean `a b` satisfies global balance for the bursty production–degradation chain.
nodes.title: Bursty expression stationary law

nodes.summary: The net probability flow into state `n` of the bursty production–degradation chain: bursts arrive at rate `κ` and add `B` molecules, `B` geometric with mean `b`, `P(B = j) = b ^ j / (1 + b) ^ (j + 1)` for `j ≥ 0`; each molecule decays at rate `γ`. A burst of size `0` changes nothing, so state `n` is left by a burst at rate `κ P(B ≥ 1) = κ b / (1 + b)`. The flow is…
nodes.title: Net probability flow of the bursty production–degradation chain

nodes.summary: Squared coefficient of variation (Brennecke et al. 2013; Svensson 2020). For a probability measure `ν` on `[0, ∞)` with square-integrable rate and `E Λ > 0`, `CV²(N) = Var N / (E N)² = 1 / E Λ + Var Λ / (E Λ)² = 1 / E Λ + CV²(Λ)`.
nodes.title: Squared coefficient of variation

nodes.summary: Zero inflation by mixing (Jensen's inequality for `λ ↦ e^{-λ}`). For a probability measure `ν` with integrable rate, `P(N = 0) = E e^{-Λ} ≥ e^{-E Λ}`, the zero class of the Poisson law with the same mean.
nodes.title: Zero inflation by mixing

nodes.summary: For `θ > 0` and `μ ≥ 0`, `P(0) = (θ / (θ + μ)) ^ θ ≥ e^{-μ}`: a negative binomial law puts at least as much mass at zero as the Poisson law with the same mean.
nodes.title: Zero class versus the Poisson law

nodes.summary: For `a > 0` and `b > 0`, the negative binomial law with size `a` and mean `a b` has `Var N / E N = 1 + b`.
nodes.title: Fano factor of bursty expression

nodes.summary: For mean `m > 0`, `Var N / E N = 1`; in particular the stationary law of the immigration–death chain has Fano factor `1`.
nodes.title: Fano factor of the Poisson law

nodes.summary: With prior `Λ ~ Gamma(a, b)` (`a, b > 0`) and one observation `N = k` from `Po(Λ)`, the posterior density (likelihood times prior over the marginal `NB(k; a, a / b)`) is the `Gamma(a + k, b + 1)` density.
nodes.title: Gamma–Poisson conjugacy, posterior

nodes.summary: For `θ > 0` and `μ ≥ 0` the negative binomial law has mean `μ`.
nodes.title: Mean

nodes.summary: For a mixing measure `ν` on `[0, ∞)` with integrable rate, `E N = E Λ` (finiteness of `ν` is not needed for this identity).
nodes.title: Mean

nodes.summary: For a mixing measure `ν` on `[0, ∞)` with square-integrable rate, `E[N (N - 1)] = E Λ²` (finiteness of `ν` is not needed for this identity).
nodes.title: Second factorial moment

nodes.summary: The negative binomial masses sum to one for `r > 0` and `p ∈ (0, 1]` (the binomial series `∑ₖ r^{(k)} xᵏ / k! = (1 - x)^{-r}` at `x = 1 - p`).
nodes.title: Negative binomial masses sum to one

nodes.summary: For `θ > 0` and `μ ≥ 0` the negative binomial masses sum to one. For `μ > 0` this is `hasSum_negBinomialPMF` transported along `negBinomialReal_eq_negBinomialPMF`, so the mean parametrization shares the canonical law's normalization instead of re-proving it.
nodes.title: Normalization

nodes.summary: For a probability measure `ν` concentrated on `[0, ∞)`, the mixed Poisson masses sum to one.
nodes.title: Normalization

nodes.summary: For `θ > 0` and `μ ≥ 0`, `E N² = μ + μ² / θ + μ²`.
nodes.title: Second moment

nodes.summary: For a finite mixing measure `ν` on `[0, ∞)` with square-integrable rate, `E N² = E Λ² + E Λ`.
nodes.title: Second moment

nodes.summary: For `γ ≠ 0` the Poisson law with mean `κ / γ` satisfies global balance for the immigration–death chain. The identity holds for all real `κ`; the chain is meaningful for `κ ≥ 0`, `γ > 0`.
nodes.title: Immigration–death stationary law

nodes.summary: The net probability flow into state `n` of the immigration–death chain on `ℕ`, in which molecules are made at rate `κ` (`n → n + 1`) and each decays at rate `γ` (`n → n - 1` at rate `γ n`): `(κ p(n - 1) + γ (n + 1) p(n + 1)) - (κ + γ n) p(n)`, with no inflow from below at `n = 0`. A law `p` is stationary (global balance) iff this flow vanishes for every `n`.
nodes.title: Net probability flow of the immigration–death chain

nodes.summary: If `X` and `Y` are independent with `P(X = j) = NB(r₁, p)(j)` and `P(Y = j) = NB(r₂, p)(j)` for all `j`, where `r₁, r₂ > 0` and `0 < p < 1`, then `P(X = k ∣ X + Y = n) = BB(n; r₁, r₂)(k)` for `k ≤ n`.
nodes.title: Negative binomial splitting for random variables

nodes.summary: For `r₁, r₂ > 0`, `0 < p < 1` and `k ≤ n`, `NB(r₁, p)(k) NB(r₂, p)(n - k) / NB(r₁ + r₂, p)(n) = BB(n; r₁, r₂)(k)`; the conditional law of one component given the total is beta-binomial and does not depend on `p`.
nodes.title: Negative binomial splitting

nodes.summary: Negative binomial mass `P(X = k) = r^{(k)} / k! · p ^ r · (1 - p) ^ k` with real shape `r` (rising factorial `r^{(k)} = (ascPochhammer ℝ k).eval r`) and success probability `p`, using the real power `p ^ r`. A probability mass function for `r > 0` and `p ∈ (0, 1]`.
nodes.title: Negative binomial mass function with real shape

nodes.summary: For `θ > 0` and `μ ≥ 0`, `negBinomialReal θ μ` is `negBinomialPMF θ p` at `p = θ / (θ + μ)`, since `1 - p = μ / (θ + μ)`. The two APIs are the same law; reuse the splitting and conditioning results proved for `negBinomialPMF` through this equivalence.
nodes.title: Mean parametrization is the canonical `p`-parametrization

nodes.summary: With mean `0` the negative binomial law is the point mass at `0`.
nodes.title: Negative binomial law with mean zero is a point mass

nodes.summary: The negative binomial mass function is nonnegative on the parameter domain.
nodes.title: Nonnegativity of the negative binomial mass function

nodes.summary: The zero class of the negative binomial law is `(θ / (θ + μ)) ^ θ`.
nodes.title: Zero class of the negative binomial law

nodes.summary: The negative binomial mass function with size `θ` and mean `μ`: `NB(k; θ, μ) = θ⁽ᵏ⁾ / k! · (θ / (θ + μ)) ^ θ · (μ / (θ + μ)) ^ k`, with the rising factorial `θ⁽ᵏ⁾ = Γ(θ + k) / Γ(θ)` and a real power `(θ / (θ + μ)) ^ θ`. The parameter domain is `θ > 0`, `μ ≥ 0`; at `μ = 0` it is the point mass at `0`. Outside the domain the formula is not a probability mass function.
nodes.title: Negative binomial mass function with size and mean

nodes.summary: The Poisson mixture over a point mass `δ_m` is the Poisson law with mean `m`.
nodes.title: Poisson mixture over a point mass is Poisson

nodes.summary: For `θ, μ > 0`, the Poisson mixture over `Gamma(θ, θ / μ)` (mean `μ`, variance `μ² / θ`) is `NB(θ, μ)`.
nodes.title: Greenwood–Yule, mean form

nodes.summary: The Poisson mixture over a Gamma rate of shape `a > 0` and rate `b > 0` is negative binomial with size `a` and mean `a / b`.
nodes.title: Greenwood–Yule

nodes.summary: The mixed Poisson mass function is nonnegative when `ν` is concentrated on `[0, ∞)`.
nodes.title: Nonnegativity of the mixed Poisson mass function

nodes.summary: The zero class of a mixed Poisson law is `E e^{-Λ}`.
nodes.title: Zero class of a mixed Poisson law

nodes.summary: The mixed Poisson mass function `p(k) = ∫ e^{-λ} λ^k / k! dν(λ)` for a mixing law `ν` of the rate. It is a probability mass function when `ν` is a probability measure concentrated on `[0, ∞)`, which the theorems below assume; for such `ν` the integrand lies in `[0, 1]`, so the integral is never a junk value.
nodes.title: Mixed Poisson mass function

nodes.summary: With prior `Λ ~ Gamma(a, b)` (`a, b > 0`) and counts `N, N'` that are independent `Po(Λ)` given `Λ`, `P(N' = j | N = k) = P(N = k, N' = j) / P(N = k) = NB(j; a + k, (a + k) / (b + 1))`.
nodes.title: Gamma–Poisson conjugacy, posterior predictive

nodes.summary: The beta-binomial masses sum to one for `α, β > 0`.
nodes.title: Beta-binomial masses sum to one

nodes.summary: For `α, β > 0`, `E M = n α / (α + β) = n π`.
nodes.title: Mean

nodes.summary: `∑_{k ≤ n} NB(r₁, p)(k) NB(r₂, p)(n - k) = NB(r₁ + r₂, p)(n)` for `p > 0` and all real shapes.
nodes.title: Convolution of negative binomial laws with a common `p`

nodes.summary: Variance (Dolzhenko–Smith parametrization). For `α, β > 0`, with `π = α / (α + β)` and `γ = 1 / (α + β + 1)`, `Var M = E M² - (E M)² = n π (1 - π) (1 + (n - 1) γ)`.
nodes.title: Variance

nodes.summary: For `θ > 0` and `μ ≥ 0` the negative binomial law has variance `μ + μ² / θ`.
nodes.title: Variance

nodes.summary: For a probability measure `ν` on `[0, ∞)` with square-integrable rate, `Var N = E N² - (E N)² = E Λ + Var Λ`: Poisson noise plus the variance of the rate.
nodes.title: Variance decomposition

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
